newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Israeli investment firms sign merger accord.
newsitem.headline: Two Israeli investment firms sign merger accord.

text.p: Ilanot Discount and Batucha Securities and Investments, two of Israel's biggest investment houses, signed a previously announced merger agreement on Monday, the companies said.
Under the deal, the joint firm will be equally controlled by Discount Investment Corp and Clal Capital Markets, a subsidiary of Clal Israel, the parent companies of Ilanot and Batucha, respectively.
The joint company will begin operations at the beginning of 1997 and manage assets worth about 3.5 billion shekels, a statement said.
Batucha is the largest non-bank brokerage in Israel, managing portfolios, provident funds and mutual funds with assets of 1.7 billion shekels. It has five branches and 118 employees.
Ilanot manages 30 mutual funds with 1.8 billion shekels in assets.
Israeli brokerage firms and fund managers have suffered from a decline in activity as a result of the prolonged slump in the Tel Aviv stock market, which has led to a number of mergers.
Shimon Elkevitch, managing director of Ilanot, will head the merged company. Micha Simion, Batucha's managing director, will leave his post, the statement said.
